note: METHOD (about 75 tool calls, 5 WebSearch). One background script queried all 76 composers: MusicBrainz (artist match on name and dates, then every work with its linked recordings), Deezer (album search on 'Given Surname' and on the surname) and, for composers where those found no chamber disc, Apple's composerTerm song search (a fuzzy match: its results must be filtered by track titles). Hits were opened through Deezer album and Apple lookup track lists, MusicBrainz recordings and releases (label, catalogue number, timings) and IMSLP work info (api.php). 14 composers had a commercial recording in scope (58 works kept, 13 of them not on IMSLP); 58 composers are 'triage: none found' and all their pages are skipped as composer triage. ADDED NOT ON IMSLP: Gassmann's oboe divertimenti H. 482, 483, 486 (CPO 2023, Supraphon, Alraune); G. F. Fuchs's Trio No. 2 for two clarinets and violin (Brilliant 96305); Fusz's Basset Horn Quartet Op. 2 (MHS 512436A, Entr'acte 2019); Hänsel's String Trios Op. 40 (RBM, Trio Anditi Köln); G. F. Giuliani's mandolin quartets Nos. 1, 3, 5 (Concerto 2036); Fodor's Quartet Op. 4 No. 5 (ReachSound.Art 2021) and Gehot's Quartet Op. 7 No. 6 (Global Village reissue 2016). LOW CONFIDENCE (the owner may drop them): Herschel's six accompanied harpsichord sonatas rest on one self-labelled disc (Herschel Ensemble, 2015; strings ad lib. in the 1769 print, recorded with violin and cello); Fodor Op. 4 No. 5 (edition not matched to IMSLP's Books 2-4 or Op. 11, key unknown); Gehot Op. 7 No. 6 (composer and opus as given by Apple Music). MATCHING CALLS. Gassmann: the 'Two Trios' page is taken as H. 377-378 (the Alraune disc plays them on two violas and bass; the pairing with the Bärenreiter edition is inferred); the NAR disc of six Gassmann quartets (Vox Aurae 1998; G, E, B-flat, D, B-flat, A, no H. numbers) matches none of the pages and is not entered; H. 482/483 are assumed to share H. 486's scoring (oboe, two violas, cello). Giordani: Op. 2 Nos. 5-6 are entered as flute quartets (the disc plays the first part on flute; the Paris print says violin); the Op. 12 flute trios as flute, viola, cello per the print. C. E. Graf: IMSLP also files him as Graaf, Christiaan Ernst, and the two Graaf pages are duplicates of the Graf pages; Nos. 4 and 6 of the no-opus set are D and F major per IMSLP's list; the keys of Op. 17 Nos. 1 and 4 are not stated anywhere I opened. F. H. Graf: the Hünteler disc numbers its quartets G, B-flat, D, A, C, G while IMSLP's Op. 5 has G major as Nos. 1 and 5 (No. 5 was printed as Wendling's Op. 10 No. 6), so the disc probably follows another print; the keys are the disc's, and only the two G-major titles carry certain Op. 5 numbers. NOT ENTERED. Arrangements: the Eroica disc of Gehot's Op. 5 trios on flute, viola and cello, Gassmann's oboe quintets H. 571/573 (after Amor und Psyche), the mandolin-ensemble transcription of Fodor's Op. 11 No. 1, Guglielmi's Bongiovanni disc (piano and orchestra version). Works not tied to a page or composer: Giordani's 'Trio No. 3 in D' (L'Apothèose, Biblioteca Nacional disc), the Giordani Op. 19 flute concertos (Columbro; with orchestra), an Op. 2 No. 3 quartet in C and a 'Chamber Quartet No. 5 in E minor' on Alba's Chydenius disc (composers not stated), a clarinet quartet in B-flat on the Kocian Quartet's Multisonic disc (composer not stated). J., and the four Gow composers (their dance-tune books are not recorded as chamber works). Fuentes Flores (a recent publication) has no recording or publisher in the lookups; not proposed for exclusion for lack of a wider search.
